land.text: the Assyrian heartland of the Middle Assyrian Empire

predecessors.note: Same state. The infobox gives "Accession of Adad-nirari II: 911 BCE"; the Middle Assyrian Empire page ends with Ashur-dan II in 912. Cliopatria switches rows at -900.

land.text: the Assyrian heartland, Harran and the lands west of the Euphrates ("Transpotamia") and the Levant that "had been split between Babylon and the Medes"

successors.note: Neo-Babylonian Empire page: Babylon took the lands west of the Euphrates and the Levant.

land.text: the northern Zagros mountains, which the Medes received

successors.note: Neo-Babylonian Empire page: "The Medes received the northern Zagros mountains."

land.text: Egypt, independent from about 655 BC under Psamtik I

successors.note: Egypt left Assyrian control long before 609; the infobox of the Neo-Assyrian page lists the Twenty-sixth Dynasty among the successors.

capitals.name: Nimrud (Kalhu)
capitals.note: "In 879 BCE, Ashurnasirpal made Nimrud the capital of the empire"; infobox "Nimrud (879–706 BCE)".

capitals.name: Dur-Sharrukin (Khorsabad)
capitals.note: Infobox "Dur-Sharrukin (706–705 BCE)"; foundations laid in 717 (Sargon II page).

capitals.name: Harran
capitals.note: Infobox "Harran (612–609 BCE)"; Ashur-uballit II's rule there "lasted until late 610 or early 609 BCE".

rulers.name: Shamshi-Adad V and Adad-nirari III
rulers.note: The page gives no reign years for these two kings; the span is what lies between Shalmaneser III's end (824) and Shalmaneser IV's start (783).

rulers.name: Sinsharishkun
rulers.note: Sin-shumu-lishir's rebellion after 627 is undated on the page and left out.

correction.text: the heartland of Assyria around Assur, Nineveh and Arbela

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -911..-901: the Neo-Assyrian Empire begins with the "Accession of Adad-nirari II: 911 BCE" but Cliopatria's Assyria row, 25,473 km2, runs to -901 and the Neo-Assyrian row starts in -900. The land is the heartland.

250,500 km2: Adad-nirari II's "wars directed to the southeast, beyond the Little Zab", Tukulti-Ninurta II's 885 march "along the Euphrates and Khabur", Ashurnasirpal II's tributaries ("including Carchemish"), Bit Adini taken in 857/856. The page gives no area before 670 and dates none of the early conquests.

correction.text: Assyria without Babylonia, which stays a separate kingdom until 729

keyframe_review.note: 482,046 km2 (-800..-751) includes 43,499 km2 of northern Babylonia (31.2 N). The pages show Babylonia as a separate kingdom until Tiglath-Pileser III "captured Babylon" in 729 (he kept it "as a full kingdom, in personal union with Assyria"), so the Babylonian part is cut out until then.

correction.text: Assyria without Babylonia until 729; later Levantine annexations in the ledger

keyframe_review.note: 479,764 km2 (-750..-701): the same Babylonian overlap (43,499 km2) is removed until 729; the Levantine additions of 740-732 (Arpad 740, Damascus 732, Galilee) and Samaria in the 720s are carried by the ledger because Cliopatria's shape does not change until -700.

correction.text: the empire without Urartu: Babylonia (729, 710), Cyprus (709), Tabal (713) and the Levant to the Egyptian border stay in; valid -700..-676

keyframe_review.note: Changed from ok to adjust on the reviewer's finding. Cliopatria's -700 shape (920,330 km2 in shapes.csv, -700..-676; 878,000 km2 on the H3 grid) holds all of Urartu as Assyrian land: 632 of the 632 cells of kingdom-of-urartu_-750 (about 160,000 km2, 37.4-46.0 E, 37.4-41.2 N) lie inside it, and Cliopatria has no Urartu shape from -700 to -616. No page gives an annexation. Urartu page: Rusa I was "crushingly defeated by Sargon II at Lake Urmia" (714); Argishti II (714-685) "restored Urartu's position against the Cimmerians, however it was no longer a threat to Assyria"; Rusa II ruled 685-645; "The Medes then took over the Urartian capital of Van in 590 BC, effectively ending the sovereignty of Urartu". Sargon II page: "Though Urartu remained powerful and Rusa retook Musasir, the 714 campaign put an end to direct confrontations"; Urzana "was forgiven and allowed to continue to govern Musasir as an Assyrian vassal"; the only annexation near this campaign is Quwe, in Anatolia. Neo-Assyrian page: "Urartu was not decisively beaten" (774). Corrected shape: the -700 shape minus the Urartu -750 shape, about 718,000 km2 on the H3 grid. (The -800 shape holds 15 cells, 3,800 km2, of the Urartu -750 shape; not worth a correction.) Babylonia (ruled directly after 729 and 710), Tabal (713) and Cyprus (709) stay in. No infobox area exists for -700 (only 670), so no ratio.

correction.text: the empire at its height ("The conquest of Egypt brought the Neo-Assyrian Empire to its greatest extent") without Upper Egypt and without Urartu; valid -675..-656

keyframe_review.note: 1,400,726 km2 against the infobox's "670 BCE: 1,400,000 km2": a match (ratio 1.00). But the shape holds all of Egypt (404,134 km2) as if directly Assyrian, and (not flagged in the first version) all of Urartu, about 160,000 km2 (632 of 632 cells of kingdom-of-urartu_-750). Upper Egypt stayed Kushite to 656; the Delta was held by vassals (ledger: the vassal state assyrian-egypt from 664); Urartu was never annexed (see the -700 verdict; at most, after Rusa II (685-645), "it became dependent on Assyria" under Sarduri III, ledger -645). Corrected -675..-656: the shape minus Upper Egypt minus Urartu, about 845,000 km2 on the H3 grid (the shape itself is 1.28 M on the grid). Against the infobox's 1.4 M that is a ratio of about 0.6, inside the factor of two; the infobox figure may count Egypt and the tributaries.

correction.text: the empire without Egypt from about 655 and without Urartu; valid -655..-621

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -655..-621 (it ran to -616 in the first version): Egypt left Assyria ("Psamtik I threw off his ties to the Assyrians circa 655 BCE"; "By 656/655 BCE, this vassal king was able to declare outright independence"). Cliopatria keeps all of Egypt in the Assyrian shape to -616 and also has an "Assyrian Egypt" row (-650..-616) that is the whole empire again. Shape = the -675 shape without Egypt and without Urartu (about 718,000 km2 on the H3 grid; Urartu was not Assyrian, see the -700 verdict). Babylonia stays in the shape as a vassal kingdom (ledger -668, -648) until Nabopolassar takes it (-626..-620).

minus.text: the empire without Egypt from about 655 and without Urartu; valid -655..-621

correction.text: the -655 shape without Babylonia, which Nabopolassar held by 620; valid -620..-616

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -620..-616, added with the -620 loss of Babylonia: "Nabopolassar's forces capture all of Babylonia in 622-620 BCE" (Neo-Assyrian page); the Neo-Babylonian page says that by 620 he "had consolidated his rule over all of Babylonia". Shape = the -655 shape minus the Babylonia -650 shape (534 cells, about 135,000 km2): about 584,000 km2 on the H3 grid. Cliopatria's -615 shape has no Babylonia either (0 shared cells). What still differs from Cliopatria's -615 shape (520,000 km2 on the grid): about 88,500 km2 of this shape lies outside it (Turkey 50,000: Tabal and Cilicia; Iraq 15,000; Lebanon 5,800 and Syria 2,800; Iran 5,000; Cyprus 4,300) and the pages date none of those losses (Tabal's later fate and the end of Cyprus are not on the pages opened).

correction.text: unchanged, valid -615..-613 (the fall of Assur and Nineveh)

keyframe_review.note: 555,850 km2 (-615..-601) is right only to the fall of the capital. Assur fell in 614 and Nineveh in 612 ("the Medes and Babylonians captured Nineveh"); the empire ends when Ashur-uballit II "was defeated at Harran in 609 BC". Valid -615..-613; the next keyframe is the rump at Harran. The step from the -620 keyframe to this shape (about 88,500 km2 of Tabal/Cilicia, Cyprus, the Phoenician coast and the Iraqi fringe, no event) is described under -620; no page dates it.

correction.text: the rump state: Harran and its region on the Balikh, plus the Levant and Syria west of the Euphrates, which no page takes from Assyria before the -609 partition; valid -612..-609

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -612..-609: after Nineveh, the rump state at Harran ("Aššur-uballiṭ's rule at Harran lasted until late 610 or early 609 BCE", Neo-Assyrian page). The Levant and Syria are kept in the shape to -609 (confidence 1, bridging a silence), on the reviewer's finding that they otherwise vanish between -615 and -612 with no event: the Neo-Babylonian page says, after the fall of Nineveh, that Babylon took "Transpotamia (the countries west of the Euphrates) and the Levant" and gives no year, and that Egypt "continued the war against Babylon for a few more years"; neo-babylonian-empire books its gain in -609 (its ledger/3). Egypt's Necho II gave "belated military support" at Harran, an Egyptian force beat Josiah at Megiddo in 609 and was beaten at Carchemish in 605 (Assyrian conquest of Egypt page), so Egyptian control of part of the Levant by 609 is possible; the pages do not say when Assyria lost it. Shape: Harran 120 km (41,700 km2) plus the -615 shape's part of the Levant region (176,000 km2), about 200,000 km2 on the grid.

ledger.note: 911 BC: Adad-nirari II becomes king of Assyria and the Neo-Assyrian Empire begins. Infobox "Accession of Adad-nirari II: 911 BCE", first king "911–891 BCE". The same state as the Middle Assyrian Empire (the Assyria dossier ends in 912).

region.text: the Jazira and the lands beyond the Little Zab won back from the Aramean kingdoms and tribes

ledger.counterpart: Aramean kingdoms and tribes (page silent on names)
ledger.note: Cliopatria's -900 shape is 250,500 km2, ten times the heartland. The page names Adad-nirari II's "wars directed to the southeast, beyond the Little Zab" and Tukulti-Ninurta II's 885 march "along the Euphrates and Khabur" but dates no conquest; the year is Cliopatria's.

region.text: Guzana (Tell Halaf) and the Khabur valley round it

ledger.note: 894 BC: Guzana pays tribute. "In 894 BCE, the Assyrian king Adad-nirari II recorded the site in his archives as a tributary Aramaean city-state" (Tell Halaf page; the sentence carries a citation-needed tag). The Bit Bahiani page gives no tribute. Mirrors bit-bahiani.
879 BC: Ashurnasirpal II makes Nimrud the capital. "In 879 BCE, Ashurnasirpal made Nimrud the capital of the empire." The court returns to Nineveh in 705 (infobox).

region.text: Bit Adini on the middle Euphrates

ledger.note: 857/856 BC: Bit Adini falls. "Ahuni of Bit Adini resisted for several years, but he surrendered to Shalmaneser in the winter of 857/856 BCE"; the city was renamed "in the summer of the next year".
808 BC: the tribute of Guzana ends in annexation (next event).

808 BC: Guzana becomes an Assyrian province. "In 808 BCE, the city and its surrounding area was reduced to a province of the Assyrian Empire"; the Bit Bahiani infobox disestablishes the kingdom in 808 BC with the Neo-Assyrian Empire as successor. Mirrors bit-bahiani.

region.text: the western and southern additions of Cliopatria's -800 shape (the Levant coast and Syria), without Babylonia

ledger.counterpart: Aram-Damascus and the western states (page silent)
ledger.note: Cliopatria widens the shape at -800 by 222,552 km2 (west to 34.5 E, south to 31.2 N). Adad-nirari III "managed to defeat Aram-Damascus" (no year) and Shamshi-Adad V beat Marduk-balassu-iqbi in 813; the page dates no annexation. The Babylonian overlap is excluded.
773 BC: Damascus pays tribute. "Shamshi-ilu captured Damascus in 773 BCE and secured tribute." The Aramean kingdom stays independent until 732.

740 BC: Tiglath-Pileser III takes Arpad. He "defeated the Urartian king Sarduri II in battle near Arpad in 743" and "Arpad was captured in 740"; "the lands controlled by Arpad were converted into two provinces and annexed".

region.text: the provinces of Kullania, Hatarikka and Simirra and the kingdom of Pattin (the page does not locate them)

ledger.note: 738 BC: new provinces in Syria. "establishing the three new provinces of Kullania, Ḫatarikka, and Ṣimirra"; Pattin was "conquered and annexed" (no year); "Hama was spared full annexation, with the kingdom being allowed to remain somewhat independent as a vassal state".

region.text: the kingdom of Hama on the Orontes

ledger.note: 738 BC: Hama is left as a vassal. "the Neo-Hittite kingdom of Hama, which he accused of plotting against him"; "Hama was spared full annexation, with the kingdom being allowed to remain somewhat independent as a vassal state".

734 BC: Gaza falls and Assyria borders Egypt. "reaching as far south as the border of Egypt"; "This campaign resulted in the conquest of Gaza"; "Assyria and Egypt shared a border for the first time in history".

region.text: Ashkelon, Judah, Edom, Moab and Ammon

ledger.note: After 734 BC: "Asqaluna, Judah, Edom, Moab and Ammon, and the Mu’na Arab tribe, all began paying tribute." The page gives no year beyond "post-734"; the end is the empire's end (page silent).
732 BC: the tribute of Damascus ends in annexation (next event).

region.text: Aram-Damascus, much of Transjordan and Galilee (the province of Megiddo)

ledger.note: 732 BC: Damascus falls. "In 732, Damascus fell and Tiglath-Pileser annexed the lands of Aram-Damascus"; "In 732 BCE, the Assyrians captured Damascus and much of Transjordan and Galilee" (Neo-Assyrian page); he divided Israel, "annexing the northern portion of the kingdom as the province Megiddo".
732 BC: southern Israel becomes a vassal. He "defeated Israel, which he divided in half", "subjugating the southern portion as a vassal kingdom".

729 BC: Tiglath-Pileser III takes Babylon. "In 729, Tiglath-Pileser captured Babylon and proclaimed himself as both king of Assyria and king of Babylon"; "Babylonia was not divided into provinces but kept as a full kingdom, in personal union with Assyria".

The 720s: Samaria falls. "Sargon claimed to have conquered the city, but it is more likely that Shalmaneser captured the city"; Israel became "the new Assyrian province of Samerina". The page gives only "the 720s"; -722 is the end of Shalmaneser V's reign.

region.text: the kingdom of Israel, the province of Samerina

ledger.note: The 720s: Samaria becomes an Assyrian province. "the new Assyrian province of Samerina"; no year on the page.
Early 721 BC: Marduk-apla-iddina seizes Babylon. "Marduk-apla-iddina had seized Babylon in early 721."

region.text: Hama and the other insurgent cities

ledger.note: 720 BC: Hama is annexed. Yahu-Bihdi's coalition is beaten at Qarqar: "Hama and the other insurgent cities were annexed again."

region.text: Hama and the other insurgent cities

ledger.note: 720 BC: Sargon II annexes Hama again after the battle of Qarqar on the Orontes.
717 BC: Sargon II retakes Carchemish. "Sargon returned to Syria in 717 to defeat an uprising led by Pisiri of Carchemish"; "In 717 BCE, Sargon retook Carchemish" (Neo-Assyrian page).

713 BC: Sargon II annexes Tabal. "In 713 Sargon campaigned against Tabal in southern Anatolia again." "Sargon deposed Ambaris, deporting him to Assyria, and annexed Tabal." His final campaign, against Tabal, was in 705, where he was killed. Cliopatria's Tabal row ends in -701 and the Assyrian -700 shape takes the land. (Re-dated by reviewer me-02 from -700, confidence 1: the Sargon II page does give the annexation.)

710 BC: Sargon II conquers Babylonia again. "In 710, Sargon decided to reconquer Babylonia"; "When Sargon marched south in 710 BCE he encountered little resistance" (Neo-Assyrian page); Dur-Yakin surrendered in 709.

709 BC: Cyprus is absorbed. "In 709, Assyria sent an expedition to Cyprus" (Sargon page); "In 709 BCE Sargon won against seven kings in the land of Ia'. Cyprus was thus absorbed into the Assyrian Empire" (Neo-Assyrian page). The greek-city-states dossier books the loss in -700 (Cliopatria's year). The Sargon II page cited here says only that "the campaign resulted in several Cypriote rulers paying tribute to Sargon" (tribute, not annexation); the pages disagree, so confidence lowered from 3 to 2 by reviewer me-02.

region.text: the Chaldean marsh land at the head of the Gulf

ledger.note: 694 BC (bridged): Chaldea is subjugated. After Nergal-ushezib's coup Sennacherib "invaded to subjugate Elam and Chaldea" and sacked Babylon (Bit-Yakin page); the page describes no annexation and the Chaldea page gives no year for the Chaldean campaign. Mirrors bit-yakin.

Esarhaddon "conquered the Phoenician city of Sidon, which was renamed Kar-Aššur‐aḫu‐iddina" (no year on the page; reign 681-669). Cliopatria's Phoenicia row leaves the Levant coast in -675 and the Assyrian shape takes it.

region.text: Scythia in West Asia, the base at Sakez near Lake Urmia

ledger.note: By 672 BC: the Scythians of West Asia become an Assyrian vassal. "By 672 BC, Bartatua had asked to marry Esarhaddon's eldest daughter"; "Thus Scythia in West Asia became a vassal and nominal extension of Assyria"; "the centre of Scythian power in West Asia shifted to Sakez near Lake Urmia". Region as in the scythia dossier. Mirrors scythia.

region.text: Egypt from the Delta to Thebes, fought over by Assyria and Kush 671-663

ledger.note: 671 BC: the Assyrian conquest of Egypt begins in earnest. "Taharqa and his army defeated the Assyrians outright in 674" (Esarhaddon raided in 673); "In 671, Esarhaddon took and sacked Memphis." Infobox 673-663 BCE.

671 BC: Memphis falls. "In 671, Esarhaddon took and sacked Memphis"; "Over all of Egypt, I appointed kings, viceroys, governors, commandants, overseers and scribes anew"; he "established Necho I as king at Sais".
669 BC: Taharqa retakes the Delta. "In 669 BC, Taharqa reoccupied Memphis, as well as the Delta."

region.text: Babylonia, ruled by Shamash-shum-ukin as king of Babylon

ledger.note: 668 BC: Babylonia passes from direct Assyrian rule to a king of its own under Ashurbanipal. "The two brothers jointly ascended to their respective thrones after Esarhaddon's death in 669"; "Shamash-shum-ukin was somewhat belatedly crowned king of Babylon in the spring of the next year" (spring 668: the page says "the next year" and does not name it). Replaces the first version's -653 loss (confidence 1, "no page dates the end of direct Assyrian rule"), which the Ashurbanipal page, already in sources, contradicts. Mirrors babylonia, whose dossier still books its gain at -653 (ledger/22) and has no keyframe for -668..-652; that dossier was not touched in this repair.

region.text: Babylonia, ruled by Shamash-shum-ukin as king of Babylon

ledger.note: 668 BC: Shamash-shum-ukin "was relegated to being Ashurbanipal's closely monitored vassal". The vassal tie runs to the revolt of 652 (next events), is renewed under Kandalanu in 648 and ends in 626. Babylonia page: Shamash-shum-ukin was installed "as a subject king in Babylon".
667 BC: Ashurbanipal wins it back. "Ashurbanipal defeated Taharqa in 667 BCE, who afterwards fled to Thebes."

c. 664 BC: Tantamani recovers Memphis. Taharqa died in 664 and "his nephew Tantamani proclaimed himself pharaoh" (Ashurbanipal page); neither page opened here says he retook Memphis, which comes from the kingdom-of-kush dossier.

region.text: the Nile Delta under Psamtik I

ledger.note: 664 BC: Psamtik becomes an Assyrian vassal. "He installed a native Egyptian Pharaoh, Psammetichus, as a vassal king in 664 BCE"; "After becoming king in 664 as a loyal Assyrian vassal" (Ashurbanipal page).
663 BC: Ashurbanipal defeats Tantamani. "This led to a renewed conflict with Ashurbanipal in 663 BCE"; "Tantamani was defeated and fled to Upper Egypt."

region.text: Egypt from the Delta to Thebes

ledger.note: 663 BC: the Assyrian conquest ends. Infobox "Assyrian victory", dates 673-663; Tantamani's authority persisted in Upper Egypt until 656.

region.text: Memphis and Lower Egypt, handed to the vassal king Psamtik I

ledger.note: 663 BC: the Delta goes to the vassal state. The first version gained Memphis and Lower Egypt from Kush (-663, above) and never gave them back, although the vassal tie of -664 covers the same land. "He installed a native Egyptian Pharaoh, Psammetichus, as a vassal king in 664 BCE"; "Psamtik I threw off his ties to the Assyrians circa 655 BCE" (Assyrian conquest of Egypt page). The gain from Kush is kept because kingdom-of-kush mirrors it (its ledger/9, -663); this loss follows it in the same year, so that after -655 the ledger no longer leaves Lower Egypt Assyrian, as the -655 keyframe says. assyrian-egypt founds its state on the same land in -664 with this state as counterpart; the one-year offset is Memphis, which Tantamani held in 664 (-664 loss above) and Ashurbanipal retook in 663. Confidence 2: the year is the retaking of Memphis, the hand-over to Psamtik is the page's 664.

c. 655 BC: Egypt leaves Assyria. "Psamtik I threw off his ties to the Assyrians circa 655 BCE"; "Egypt already regained independence in the middle of Ashurbanipal's reign" (Ashurbanipal page). Egypt's Twenty-sixth Dynasty continues the land.

region.text: Susa, sacked after the Battle of the Ulai

ledger.note: 653 BC: Assyria occupies Susa without annexing Elam. Elam page: after the battle of the Ulai, "Susa itself was sacked and occupied by the Assyrians". The Ashurbanipal page, already in sources, has the defeats (665, 653, 647-646) and the plunder of Susa but no occupation, and says "Ashurbanipal did not annex Elam, instead leaving it to its own devices"; the pages disagree, hence confidence 2. The elam dossier (me-01) books an occupation from 653 and then an annexation from 640 to 612 with this state as counterpart; this dossier books only the short occupation (next, -646) and no annexation.

region.text: Babylonia, ruled by Shamash-shum-ukin as king of Babylon

ledger.note: 652 BC: the vassal king rises against his brother. "Shamash-shum-ukin revolted in 652" (Ashurbanipal page; the Neo-Assyrian page adds "with the aid of several Elamite kings"). The land is contested from the same year (next event).
652 BC: Shamash-shum-ukin revolts. "in 652 BCE he revolted with the aid of several Elamite kings."
648 BC: Ashurbanipal takes Babylon. "In 648 BCE Ashurbanipal captured Babylon after a long siege."
648 BC: Babylonia becomes an Assyrian vassal kingdom. "Babylon fell in 648, after a siege lasting two years"; Kandalanu, "a new vassal king of Babylon", is counted from 647 and died in 627.

region.text: Susa, sacked on the return from the 646 campaign

ledger.note: 646 BC (bridged): the occupation of Susa closes with the last dated Assyrian act there. "the Assyrian forces brutally plundered Susa" on the return from the 646 campaign (Ashurbanipal page); Elam page: "In 646 BC Ashurbanipal devastated Susiana with ease, and sacked Susa". No page says when an occupation ended or that Susa was held to 640 or 612: "Ashurbanipal did not annex Elam, instead leaving it to its own devices" (Ashurbanipal page); he "chose to not annex and integrate Elam" (Neo-Assyrian page).

645 BC: Urartu becomes a dependent of Assyria, not a province. After Rusa II (685-645) "it became dependent on Assyria"; Sarduri III (645-635) called Ashurbanipal his "father" (Urartu page; the infobox dates Sarduri III 639-635). Booked on the suzerain only, as the schema asks. Urartu was never annexed (see the -700 keyframe).
635 BC (bridged): the end of Sarduri III's reign. The page says nothing of a tie after him (Erimena "possibly ruling from 635 to 620 BC", Rusa III 620-609); the Medes took Van in 590.

Nov. 626 BC: Babylon is lost for good. "Nabopolassar was formally invested as king of Babylon in November 626 BCE, restoring Babylonia as an independent kingdom"; the city "was seized by Nabopolassar in 626 and never again fell into Assyrian hands".

Nov. 626 BC: Nabopolassar's revolt takes ground. "Nippur was recaptured in October 626 BCE" and he "was formally invested as king of Babylon in November 626 BCE" (Neo-Assyrian page); Neo-Babylonian page: "In 626 BC, Nabopolassar assaulted and successfully seized the cities of Babylon and Nippur". He held only these two cities at first; the rest of Babylonia is contested until 620 (next events). Confidence 2: the year is the page's, the zone is the whole of Babylonia as the reviewer proposed.

region.text: Scythia in West Asia, the base at Sakez near Lake Urmia

ledger.note: 625 BC (bridged): the Scythian tie ends. "In 625 BC, the Median king Cyaxares invited the Scythian leaders to a feast", and "Scythia supported the Medo-Babylonian conquests of Assur in 614 BC, of Nineveh in 612 BC"; the page does not say when the vassalage ended, so the end is bridged to the 625 feast as in the scythia dossier. Mirrors scythia.

region.text: the rest of Babylonia, outside Babylon and Nippur

ledger.note: 620 BC: the fighting for Babylonia ends. Neo-Assyrian page: Nabopolassar's forces "capture all of Babylonia in 622-620 BCE"; Neo-Babylonian page: by 620 he "had consolidated his rule over all of Babylonia".

region.text: the rest of Babylonia, outside Babylon and Nippur

ledger.note: 620 BC: Babylonia is lost for good. The vassal tie ended in -626 with Babylon and Nippur only; the pages date the rest to 620 ("all of Babylonia in 622-620 BCE", Neo-Assyrian page; "In 620 BC Nabopolassar seized control over much of Babylonia", Babylonia page: "with the support of most of the inhabitants", "only the city of Nippur and some northern regions" staying loyal to Assyria). Mirrors neo-babylonian-empire (its ledger/1, -620), which had no counterpart here in the first version. Confidence 2: the pages disagree between 622-620, 620, "all" and "much".

Late 615 or 614 BC: the Medes take Assur. "The Medes mounted attacks on both Nimrud and Nineveh and captured Assur." Neo-Babylonian page: attacks "in July or August 614 BC" ending with the siege of Assur.

612 BC: Nineveh falls. "In 612 BCE, after a siege lasting two months, the Medes and Babylonians captured Nineveh." Neo-Babylonian page: June to August 612, the walls breached in August. Babylon took the heartland; the Medes received "the northern Zagros mountains".

region.text: Ashkelon, Judah, Edom, Moab and Ammon

ledger.note: The tributaries of 734 (Judah, Edom, Moab, Ammon, Ashkelon) are closed at the empire's end; the pages give no year when each stopped paying (Judah fell to Babylon in 587 per the Neo-Babylonian page).

region.text: the Levant and Syria west of the Euphrates ("Transpotamia")

ledger.note: 609 BC (bridged): the west passes to Babylon. "Babylon took Transpotamia (the countries west of the Euphrates) and the Levant" after the partition; the page gives no year. The first version had no event between the -615 shape (which holds the Levant to 28 N) and the Harran circle of -612; the reviewer offered to book the loss to the Twenty-sixth Dynasty of Egypt about -616..-609, but no page opened says Egypt took the Levant from Assyria before Megiddo (609) and Carchemish (605). The land therefore stays in the -612 keyframe to -609 and goes to neo-babylonian-empire, which books the same gain in -609 (its ledger/3). For Egypt's share (Josiah killed at Megiddo, 609), see twenty-sixth-dynasty-of-egypt (me-03).

region.text: Harran and its region, the last Assyrian land

ledger.note: 609 BC: the Assyrian state ends at Harran. Infobox "Fall of Harran: 609 BCE"; Ashur-uballit II "was defeated at Harran in 609 BC" and "the territory of the Neo-Assyrian Empire had been split between Babylon and the Medes" (Neo-Babylonian page).

wars.name: Ahuni and the conquest of Bit Adini
wars.outcome: "Ahuni of Bit Adini resisted for several years, but he surrendered to Shalmaneser in the winter of 857/856 BCE."
wars.note: The page gives the surrender, not the start of the war.

wars.name: Battle of Qarqar
wars.outcome: "In 853 BCE, a coalition of western states assembled at Tell Qarqur in Syria against Assyrian expansion"; Assyrian forces "thrice tried to capture Damascus but were unsuccessful" (undated).
wars.note: No territorial result on the page.

wars.name: Shamshi-ilu's wars with Urartu and Damascus
wars.outcome: "In 774 BCE, Shamshi-ilu scored an important victory against Argishti I of Urartu", who was "not decisively beaten"; "Shamshi-ilu captured Damascus in 773 BCE and secured tribute".

wars.name: Tiglath-Pileser III's Syrian and Levantine campaigns

zones.text: Arpad (740), Hama (738), Gaza (734), Damascus and Galilee (732)

wars.outcome: Arpad fell in 740 after a three-year siege and became two provinces; Hama became a vassal in 738; Gaza fell in 734; Damascus and the northern half of Israel were annexed in 732.

wars.name: Fall of Samaria
wars.outcome: Probably taken by Shalmaneser V in the 720s; "Sargon claimed to have conquered the city". Israel became the province of Samerina.
wars.note: Years are Shalmaneser V's reign (727-722); the page gives only "the 720s".

wars.name: Revolt of Hama and the Battle of Qarqar (720)
wars.outcome: Sargon beat Yahu-Bihdi's coalition at Qarqar on the Orontes and annexed Hama again; Hanunu of Gaza rebelled in the same period.

wars.name: Sargon II's Urartu campaign
wars.outcome: "The 714 campaign put an end to direct confrontations between Urartu and Assyria for the rest of Sargon's reign"; Musasir was plundered.
wars.note: No annexation: Urartu "remained powerful and Rusa retook Musasir" (Sargon II page); Cliopatria's Assyrian shapes of -700 and -675 swallow Urartu, which the keyframes now cut out.

wars.name: Sargon II's Cyprus expedition
wars.outcome: "In 709, Assyria sent an expedition to Cyprus"; seven kings of Ia' were beaten and "Cyprus was thus absorbed into the Assyrian Empire".

wars.name: Sennacherib's Levantine campaign
wars.outcome: "In 701 BCE Sennacherib undertook the most famous campaign of his reign, invading the Levant"; the page gives no territorial result (Judah is a tributary).

wars.name: Sennacherib's Elamite and Babylonian wars
wars.outcome: "In 694 BCE Sennacherib invaded Elam"; "Sennacherib finally recaptured Babylon in 689 BCE," and "Babylon was destroyed".

wars.name: Assyrian conquest of Egypt

zones.text: Egypt from the Delta to Thebes

wars.outcome: Assyrian victory: Memphis fell in 671, the Delta swung in 669 and 667, Psamtik became a vassal in 664, Tantamani was beaten in 663; "The Neo-Assyrian Empire vassalised Egypt for a period of about 10 years".

wars.name: Assyrian wars with Elam
wars.outcome: "Elam was defeated in a series of conflicts in 665, 653 and 647–646"; Susa was "captured and devastated"; but "Ashurbanipal did not annex Elam, instead leaving it to its own devices".
wars.note: Pages disagree: the Elam page has Susa "sacked and occupied by the Assyrians" in 653 and Humban-Haltash III captured in 640, when Ashurbanipal "annexed and destroyed the country"; the Ashurbanipal page says he "did not annex Elam, instead leaving it to its own devices" and the Neo-Assyrian page that he "chose to not annex and integrate Elam". The ledger books a short occupation of Susa (-653 to -646, from the Elam page) and no annexation; the elam dossier (me-01) should drop its -640 to -612 annexation and the occupation after -646.

wars.name: Revolt of Shamash-shum-ukin
wars.outcome: Ashurbanipal captured Babylon in 648 after a siege of two years; Kandalanu was installed as vassal king.

wars.name: Fall of the Assyrian Empire

zones.text: Babylonia, contested 626-620 between the Assyrian vassal tie and Nabopolassar

wars.outcome: Nabopolassar won Babylon (626), the Medes took Assur (614), the Medes and Babylonians took Nineveh (612), and Ashur-uballit II was beaten at Harran in 609.
wars.note: Egypt's Necho II gave "belated military support" at Harran (Assyrian conquest of Egypt page). Babylonia is a separate contest from -626 to -620 (ledger); the Levant stays in the rump state to -609 only because no page dates its loss.

certainty.note: Every frontier is approximate; the Egyptian border of 734 ("as far south as the border of Egypt") and the Median-Babylonian partition are the only lines the pages mention.

notes:
IDENTITY. One state with assyria (Middle Assyrian), split only at Cliopatria's row boundary: the Neo-Assyrian Empire begins in -911 (accession of Adad-nirari II) while Cliopatria's Assyria shape runs to -901; the keyframe neo-assyrian-empire_-911 fills -911..-901. The dossier ends in -609 (Harran), 8 years after the last big Cliopatria shape ends in -601 and 6 after Nineveh.
AREA. Infobox "670 BCE: 1,400,000 km2" vs Cliopatria 1,400,726 km2 for -675..-616: ratio 1.00. But that shape contains all of Egypt (404,134 km2) in every year to -616, and a duplicate "Assyrian Egypt" row (-650..-616) that repeats the whole empire; see assyrian-egypt.
PAGES. 9 pages (budget 5): Neo-Assyrian Empire, Tiglath-Pileser III, Sargon II, Ashurbanipal, Assyrian conquest of Egypt (shared with assyrian-egypt), plus Neo-Babylonian Empire (shared with neo-babylonian-empire) for the fall, Scythians (opened only to mirror the scythia dossier's vassal events -672 and -625), Tell Halaf and Bit Yakin (opened for the bit-bahiani and bit-yakin dossiers and mirrored here at -894/-808 and -694). Shalmaneser III was opened for the bit-adini dossier and has nothing on Bit Adini, Til Barsip or Bit Agusi (only Carchemish tribute, Damascus 841, Marduk-bel-ushate 851, Qarqar 853). Not opened: Ashurnasirpal II, Adad-nirari II/III, Sennacherib, Esarhaddon; hence the early reconquest, -800 and -675 events are confidence 1.
CONFLICTS WITH OTHER DOSSIERS. (1) elam (me-01) books an Assyrian occupation of Susa -653..-640, the annexation of Susiana -640 and a return -612; Ashurbanipal's page says Elam was not annexed (defeats 665, 653, 647-646). REPAIR: the Elam page itself says "sacked and occupied" (653) and "annexed and destroyed the country" (640); this dossier now books only a short occupation of Susa, -653..-646, and no annexation (see REPAIR). (2) greek-city-states books Cyprus in -700; the pages opened here give 709. (3) kingdom-of-kush books the Egyptian swings -671..-663 against this state: mirrored here (the -664 loss at confidence 1: not on the pages opened). (4) Cliopatria's NA shape includes 43,499 km2 of northern Babylonia from -800 (cut out until -729) and 118 k km2 at -700 (kept: the pages have Babylonia ruled directly from 729 and again from 710).
FOR OTHER DOSSIERS. mitanni (me-04): Hanigalbat annexed by Assyria; median-kingdom (me-05): Assur 614; twenty-sixth-dynasty-of-egypt (me-03): independent Egypt from about 655, not from -615; kingdom-of-israel / kingdom-of-judah / philistia (me-04): the 732-720s annexations and the post-734 tributaries; tabal-kingdom, phoenicia (me-04). Counterparts without a dossier: Arpad, Hama, Aram-Damascus, Pattin, Carchemish, the Aramean kingdoms of the Jazira.
GAZETTEER. Names the gazetteer lacks: Gaza (used as a coordinate), Hama and Carchemish and Bit Adini (coordinates), Tell Qarqur. Region "Damascus (region)", "Aleppo (region)", "Samaria", "Roman Judaea", "Canaan", "Nile Valley (Egypt)", "Upper Egypt", "Lower Egypt" exist.
DISAGREEMENTS. Fall of Assur 615/614; Harran 610/609; Samaria Shalmaneser V or Sargon; Susa 648/647/646. Egypt: Neo-Assyrian page "vassalised Egypt for about 10 years" vs Cliopatria's 34 years of Assyrian Egypt.
REPAIR (2026-10-18, after the reviewer's fail verdict). (a) URARTU: Cliopatria's -700 and -675 shapes hold all of Urartu (632 of 632 cells of kingdom-of-urartu_-750); -700 is now adjust and the -700, -675 and -655 corrections subtract that shape; ledger -645/-635 books Urartu as a dependent of Assyria under Sarduri III (Urartu page), not as annexed land. (b) DELTA: a -663 loss of Memphis and Lower Egypt to assyrian-egypt follows the gain from Kush (kept, because kingdom-of-kush mirrors it). (c) BABYLONIA: the -653 loss is replaced by a -668 loss plus vassal_start (Ashurbanipal page: Shamash-shum-ukin crowned the spring after 669, a "closely monitored vassal"), a -652 vassal_end, and the existing -652/-648 contest and -648 vassal; babylonia (not touched) still needs the -668 gain, a -668..-652 keyframe and the -652 events. (d) -626..-620: contest_start (Nov. 626) and contest_end plus loss (620) with neo-babylonian-empire; a new keyframe -620..-616 drops Babylonia. (e) LEVANT: kept in the new -612..-609 keyframe and lost to neo-babylonian-empire in -609 at confidence 1; the Egyptian option was not taken because no page opened has Egypt take the Levant before Megiddo (609). (f) ELAM: short occupation -653..-646 booked (schema direction: this state occupies elam's land); no annexation. Pages opened for the repair: Urartu, Elam, Babylonia (second page only); re-read: Sargon II, Assyrian conquest of Egypt, Ashurbanipal, Neo-Babylonian Empire, Neo-Assyrian Empire (12 pages in all, budget 5).
